clinical_observations.content: Sabrina participated in an in-clinic evaluation with her mother present. She presented as cheerful and generally cooperative, although she displayed intermittent shifts in attention and moderately high levels of distractibility. Her muscle tone was within normal limits, and her range of motion was adequate across all assessed joints. Sabrina demonstrated better task engagement during self-directed activities and required maximal verbal and visual cues to sustain attention during structured tasks. Fine motor coordination was emerging, and she frequently needed hand-over-hand assistance to complete tasks, indicating challenges with visual-motor integration. Her engagement decreased without consistent assistance, and standardized testing involved modifications to optimize her performance and ensure accurate representation of her abilities. Notably, Sabrina's ability to sustain focus was most challenged with longer activities, affecting the overall validity of some standardized measures.
